Subject: Draft - shed redo post (hold till I add the pics)

Two Saturdays, one shed, and a list that reads like a horror story.

A buddy of mine had power run out to his shed. Not a garage, not a workshop — a shed. Here's what was waiting when I opened the panel:

• 3 orange extension cords daisy chained together, out a basement window, across the yard, under the deck
• one splice wrapped in DUCT TAPE. Not electrical tape. Duct tape
• a 30 amp breaker feeding 14 gauge wire
• a speaker wire feeding a regular outlet
• a "GFCI" that was a regular outlet with a GFCI sticker stuck on the side
• a ceiling fan box held up by one drywall screw
• a mouse nest inside the junction box. The mice were fine. Completely unbothered
• inside the panel door, in sharpie: SHED - DONT TOUCH - RON

And the wife standing there goes, "Who's Ron?" Like I should know. Nobody did. Ron, if you're reading this, your shed is a landmark now and I'm sorry about the mice.

I want to be fair about this. The guy wasnt evil, he was cheap and a little proud, and that's most of these. He didn't know what he didn't know. Everybody starts somewhere, I been there.

But three extension cords daisy chained is not a shortcut, it's a countdown. That splice under the deck was one hot night away from taking the house with it, and I'd rather not say that about somebody I like.

What we did: trenched 18 inches, pulled 12/2 UF, 20 amp GFCI breaker, real box, real outlets, fan on a proper brace. Permit, inspection, all of it. Paid in 2 pizzas and a case of Yuengling, so don't get too excited about my rates.

Here's the part I actually care about. If you've got a buddy who watched a bunch of YouTube videos and wants to do your electrical for $150 cash this weekend, please don't. I'm not offended, I'm serious. I've seen what that cord was doing under that deck, and I know what yours is doing right now. In PA this work has to be done by a licensed electrician with a permit and an inspection, for good reason. Unpermitted electrical is how houses burn down, and how an insurance claim turns into "well, we have to deny this." And a shock kills just as dead as a fire, with no medal for it.

Call a licensed guy. Not your buddy with a YouTube video.

Test everything. I'm not even joking anymore.

26 years and the only thing that's ALWAYS true is somebody's uncle wired it.
